notes.note: Eight or sixteen directions? Pick sixteen. Each way a line can run is a path through the garden, and enchanted dishes coming alive is my kind of kitchen.
A dark factory in a cloud box. That sounds sterile to me. Is it smart thinking? It is thinking, at least. Plant herbs in there and I'll be won over.
'Too many' is what every cottage garden says, and it is right. The Nutcracker worries me: machinery runs cold. Give him a pot of mint and see if he stays gentle.
Guardians of the Vibes. Not one root in it, and it smells of a shop. Paul is right, and I would have said it with more thorns.
A gallery opened a few colors at a time: that is how a garden works, one bud, then the next. Paul, that is grown, not stocked. I resent how right it is.
Tone the Georgian down, gently: yes. Just don't pull out the herbs. A thread can be thin, but a kitchen garden with no herbs is only a lawn.

favorite_idea.why: A marginarium is where herbals keep their best scribbles, so a book of stories growing in its margins is the most garden-like idea in the lot.

steer: Keep the margins short and warm, let the guardians disagree a little, and let the hand-made parts of the day show more than the factory does.
